svg.title: Wage Garnishment and Bank Levy Go/No-Go Gates
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-garnishment-and-levy-gates; chapter number: 5; chart type: decision_tree; title: Wage Garnishment and Bank Levy Go/No-Go Gates; subtitle: Four checks before relying on the state's collection machinery; caption: The creditor must locate a job or bank, run the interest math, anticipate exemption fights, and stop cold on a bankruptcy notice; Mr. Grey's answer to thin accounts is a four-bank levy.; assumptions note: Gate order is an organizing sequence built from the cited operator gates; exemption amounts and caps are state-specific as reported for Arizona and Georgia.; note: Sources - Consumer Warrior with John Skiba (YmCEqLCbD3s), Law Office of Jeffrey B. Kelly (cHsptp1ujiI), Westgate Law (Nb1quOaLNWk), Mr. Grey Judgment Enforcement (CLxNTh8V1qQ), Bobby Benjy (a13Ojjc6ruw).; nodes: gate: G1; question: Has a job or bank account been located for the debtor?; pass next: G2; fail action: Mine the credit report for employment and the old check or auto-debit trail for the bank, including spouse-name and joint accounts.; gate: G2; question: Does the garnishment outpace 28 to 30 percent contract interest?; pass next: G3; fail action: Do not rely on a 10 percent Arizona wage garnishment alone; add bank levies, and confirm a Georgia employer computes withholding correctly.; gate: G3; question: Is the frozen money free of exemptions?; pass next: G4; fail action: Expect fights over all-Social Security accounts, the roughly $5,600 Arizona account exemption that doubles for married couples, and adult-child money in joint accounts.; gate: G4; question: Is the file clear of any bankruptcy notice?; pass next: Fire a four-bank levy at once and let any overage flow back to the debtor.; fail action: Stop enforcement, return money taken after the filing, and track the sheriff and the bank.

text.title: Wage Garnishment and Bank Levy Go/No-Go Gates
text.tspan: Wage Garnishment and Bank Levy Go/No-Go Gates

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Has a job or bank account been located for the debtor?; pass next: G2; fail action: Mine the credit report for employment and the old check or auto-debit trail for the bank, including spouse-name and joint accounts.

gate: G2; question: Does the garnishment outpace 28 to 30 percent contract interest?; pass next: G3; fail action: Do not rely on a 10 percent Arizona wage garnishment alone; add bank levies, and confirm a Georgia employer computes withholding correctly.

gate: G3; question: Is the frozen money free of exemptions?; pass next: G4; fail action: Expect fights over all-Social Security accounts, the roughly $5,600 Arizona account exemption that doubles for married couples, and adult-child money in joint accounts.

gate: G4; question: Is the file clear of any bankruptcy notice?; pass next: Fire a four-bank levy at once and let any overage flow back to the debtor.; fail action: Stop enforcement, return money taken after the filing, and track the sheriff and the bank.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order is an organizing sequence built from the cited operator gates; exemption amounts and caps are state-specific as reported for Arizona and Georgia.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Gate order is an organizing sequence built from the cited operator gates; exemption amounts and caps are state-specific
as reported for Arizona and Georgia.
